business_process: Remote patient monitoring and secondary alarm notification
description: Device cloud receives telemetry from PM-2 and PM-1 monitors; clinicians view patients remotely; secondary alarm notifications and results go to hospital EHRs and clinical communication systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 40 hospitals rely on remote viewing and secondary alarms for about 8900 monitors; primary alarms still sound at the bedside, which caps safety impact at Moderate; BAAs and customer contracts carry availability commitments; data older than 15 minutes is not useful for remote monitoring
manual_workaround: Hospitals revert to bedside alarms and in-person rounding under their own downtime procedures; monitors buffer 72 hours of data locally and resend when the service returns; Customer Support Manager calls each hospital's clinical engineering contact
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider (subcontractor BA); hospital networks and EHRs; identity provider vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Cloud Operations Lead; 14 cloud and DevOps engineers; Customer Support Manager

description: Update service delivers signed PM-2 firmware images to fielded monitors; field service loads PM-1 updates by USB
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An out-of-cycle security fix must reach the field as soon as possible under 524B(b)(2)(B) and within the 60-day window in FDA's postmarket guidance; routine releases can wait days; images are rebuilt from the repository, so a 24-hour RPO is enough
manual_workaround: Field service engineers install urgent fixes by USB at hospitals; hospitals apply compensating network controls from the customer advisory
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (update service; object storage); SYS-04; SYS-11

description: Hospital calls and tickets; troubleshooting; on-site repairs and installations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hospitals expect same-day response for monitors in clinical use; support calls are often the first sign of a complaint or a security event
manual_workaround: Phone line forwarded to support staff mobile phones; paper call log copied into the ticketing system and eQMS when restored
dependent_third_parties: Support ticketing vendor (subcontractor BA); phone carrier

business_process: PM-2 production (Line 1 board test; Line 2 final assembly and final test)
description: Build, test, and release monitors; test stations load signed firmware and device identity certificates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $232000 of revenue per business day; a two-week finished-goods buffer covers normal orders; device history records must be complete before release (21 CFR 820); the MES configuration changes rarely, so a daily backup is enough
manual_workaround: Ship from finished-goods stock; hold lots until MES records can be completed; no paper test records are allowed for release

business_process: Order fulfillment, shipping, and UDI traceability
description: Orders; shipping; serial number and UDI records that trace each unit to its hospital
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Traceability by serial number is needed to find every affected unit in a correction or removal (21 CFR 806); shipping delays affect revenue but not patients
manual_workaround: Manual shipping log on paper; enter into the ERP when restored

description: Complaint intake and investigation; medical device reports; correction and removal reports; business associate breach notices to hospitals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Regulatory clocks run in days: 5 work days (803.53), 10 working days (806.10), 30 calendar days (803.50), and 60 calendar days or shorter BAA terms for breach notice (164.410); complaint records must not be lost
manual_workaround: Paper complaint form and a spreadsheet log kept by Quality; FDA electronic submissions can be prepared from a clean laptop
dependent_people_or_facilities: 18 quality and regulatory staff; Compliance Manager (Privacy Officer)

description: Repair and refurbish returned monitors; reload firmware
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Returned units can wait; loaner pool covers hospitals
manual_workaround: Ship loaners from stock; defer repairs

business_process: Device and cloud software engineering, build, and code signing
description: Develop, build, test, and sign PM-2 firmware and device cloud releases
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No security fix can ship without the build pipeline and the code-signing key; the key has one copy and no escrow (R-025), so its loss would stop every PM-2 update
manual_workaround: Engineers keep working on local clones; releases wait for the build server and signing key

description: Design history files; risk management files; 510(k) and AI-001 submission preparation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Submission dates are planned months ahead; records must be complete for FDA inspection
manual_workaround: Work from exported documents; defer approvals

business_process: Product security vulnerability intake and coordinated disclosure
description: security@ mailbox; researcher and ISAO reports; CISA advisories; vulnerability triage and customer advisories
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An exploited vulnerability is a patient-safety and regulatory event; FDA's postmarket guidance sets 30-day customer communication for uncontrolled risk; a lost report can lead to uncoordinated public disclosure (R-003)
manual_workaround: Researchers and hospitals reach the Product Security Lead by the phone number in the CVD policy; triage continues in a spreadsheet

description: Payables; receivables; payroll; onboarding and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; missing payroll has legal and retention impact; same-day access removal at termination depends on HR tickets
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the payroll provider; HR calls the IT Manager to disable accounts
